intended_object: On each open set U of a manifold M modelled over a nontrivially normed field 𝕜, the canonical ring homomorphism C(U, 𝕜) → C⁰(U, 𝕜) that sends a continuous scalar function to itself, viewed as a section of the sheaf of order-0 differentiable functions. Continuity is the same as 0-times differentiability. Inferred from the docstring, and from the later use of this map as the component on U of the sheaf isomorphism (line 470).
explanation: The map sends a continuous function f to the pair ⟨f, proof that f is 0-times differentiable⟩, using `contMDiff_zero_iff`, which says 0-times differentiable means continuous. The function itself is left unchanged. All the ring-homomorphism axioms are proved with `Subtype.ext` and `rfl`, so they hold because the map is the identity on the underlying functions. This is the expected identity map that compares continuous functions with order-0 differentiable functions. The library proves that it has a two-sided inverse (`zeroToContinuous`) and that it is compatible with restriction to smaller open sets. It then assembles these maps over all U into the sheaf isomorphism. The setting is the natural one: any nontrivially normed field and any manifold with corners. Mathlib does not have this particular comparison map between section rings, and the map is correct.
